utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is Tuesday, the 29th of January, 2008. Good morning, Ms. Dahl; good morning, Mr. Seselj; and my greetings to all the people helping us out. We will in a few moments have the witness brought in; but before he comes in, I'm going to ask the registrar to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, we are in open session. Mr. Seselj, I believe you wanted to speak to two topics. The first topic has to do with quality of expert of the coming witness. The Trial Chamber is very clear on this. In your submissions, you challenged his quality as an expert. The Trial Chamber issued a decision stating in paragraph 17. I'm going to read it out to you so that you be fully appraised of it and to avoid wasting time. "The Trial Chamber considers on the basis of the objections raised by the accused that the witness is to appear before this Tribunal to answer the questions by the Prosecution, the accused, and maybe the Chamber. During cross-examination, the accused will have an opportunity to challenge the probative value, the relevance, and the credibility of the conclusions of the expert." In paragraph 18, we conclude this: "In the light of the testimony of the witness, the Trial Chamber will consider the relevance and probative value of his report and will rule on the admission of the report into evidence." In other words, he will be put questions by the Prosecution, you'll have the cross-examination to put your questions to him, the Judges will do so as well; and, only after that, will there be a finite ruling on this. So there's no need for a debate before, beforehand, since this discussion will be settled upon his testimony after the cross-examination. So this is the first topic I wanted to raise. Personally speaking, let me add this. The Rules, which is a binding document, is inspired by the common-law system in which you have expert witnesses who come upon the request of parties without having the Judges saying anything beforehand. It's true that in another civil -- law system you would not have this waste of time. In another legal system where Judges appoint independent expert witnesses who come to testify with an adversarial discussion by the parties, after that only, we would save a lot of time, but for reasons that escape me another system was preferred in which the Prosecution has their experts and you, yourself, will have yours. The Trial Chamber will rule on the merits of the expert testimony after that when the documents will be tendered into evidence. This is what I want to say as to the expert issue which is a recurrent one. Each time we have to intervene on this. We have a very well-defined type of proceedings. The expert report will only be admitted after there has been a discussion and adversarial debate. So that's the first topic. As to the second topic, I believe you have some press cutting. I can't translate it because it's in your language. So is -- with regard to this second topic, what did you want to say, Mr. Seselj? I remind you, however, that if you want to tackle a confidential issue, you have to ask yourself for a private session since I don't know beforehand what you want to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will not be referring to anything of a confidential nature. I have had four issues to raise today; and regarding these two, I informed Mr. Doriswamy of them because I asked that some documents be copied for the Trial Chamber and for the Prosecutor. First of all, as far as Yves Tomic is concerned, I have provided you with five documents from which you can see that he cannot be an impartial expert of the Prosecution in this case. And I draw your attention to two decisions of the International Court for Rwanda; and in its decision dated the 11th of November, 2003, the Trial Chamber notes, and I quote: "An expert witness has to testify fully respecting scientific objectivity." And in the case of Prosecutor versus Akayesu, the request for the Defence regarding a high-quality expert witness and the Trial Chamber says, and I quote, that: "The expert witness authorised to testify must not only be of repute in his profession, but must also be impartial in the case." Both these decisions were confirmed by the Appeals Chamber of the Rwanda Tribunal in 2007 in the case Rugambarara, paragraph 199 of the judgement. I have supplied you with five articles by Mr. Tomic, from which it can be seen that he is an ideologically passionate opponent of the Serbian Radical Party of which I'm still the president, and this was confirmed at the party congress in 2006. He uses political terms such as extremist, nationalist, ultra-nationalist, and he's a member of a political organization which is called, The French Association for Studies of the Balkans, which is conducting an anti-Serbian campaign and is engaged in destructive political activity and a member is the Montenegrin prince, Nikola Petrovic-Njegos, who has pretensions to the Montenegrin throne. This delegation was -- consistently advocated the break-up of the association of Serbia and Montenegro, so that he's involved in the break-up of Yugoslavia, in the break-up of Serbia, and I have provided you and the members of the Trial Chamber with these documents to show that I have evidence that he is not neutral and impartial. But it is up to you. I am in your hands, and I am ready for the cross-examination. That is the first point. Regarding the second point, I think it is very important for you to have in mind that Natasa Kandic has in public in the Serbian press denied calling Witness Stoparic during his testimony, and she even stated that this was a fabrication of the Serbian Radical Party. As we spoke about this in a public session, I insist once again that I be provided with a complete transcript of the message sent by Natasa Kandic to Goran Stoparic during his testimony, and I request that the Trial Chamber consider whether there are reasons to institute proceedings against Natasa Kandic because as a close associate of The Hague Prosecutor's office, she was well aware that she must not influence witnesses in any way and -- in general, and especially not during their testimony. This is the other problem that I wanted to raise. Of course, I have provided you with the documents, but you can decide whether to start contempt of court proceedings. Another point I wish to raise is that you have issued four subpoenas for Defence witnesses to be brought to testify in the Prosecution case. Those witnesses have objected to the subpoenas; and immediately after that, I don't know whether you ruled about these objections, you issued instructions for free passage. The key issue in the objections is the request for re-consideration of the subpoenas, since they personally have informed you that they are Defence witnesses. If you reject that objection, then you can issue the instructions that you have already started to issue. Maybe I'm not fully informed. All I know is about these instructions for free passage. I'm not mentioning the name of the witness or his pseudonym. I'm just raising the issue as a matter of principle, and I don't know how to deal with it. And the fourth problem, the Prosecution is again bombarding me with the requests for various 92 bis and other forms of testimony. Recently you provided me with your decision rejecting a large number of Prosecution requests, but some of them you left to decide upon later, after hearing my reactions to them. I think that I have stated my views about all of these once and for all. I will never accept testimony of witnesses under 92 bis, ter, et cetera. The way the Prosecution interprets this rule applies to quite different cases. This time I wish to underline that Witness Goran Stoparic, by his public and direct testimony in the courtroom, absolutely disqualified the practice of the Prosecution regarding the taking of statements. You can read all his statements and the transcript of his testimony, and you will see the enormous gap between them. From this we can conclude that the Prosecution can never be trusted that any statement is trustworthy. To come to the courtroom and say he signed it, but he has no idea what he signed. You saw that Mr. Stoparic, who is not a stupid man, who is quite an intelligent man in view of his level of education, he could not recall many of the things that he signed in the statement and then he denied them. And I think this practice should be disqualified once and for all, and that has only added to my conviction that I should not accept any witnesses under 92 bis and ter. If you accept any such statements, I will treat it as if it was non-existent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly on these four topics. The first one, the expert witness, following what I said earlier on, you now are saying that this expert is allegedly not impartial, as expressed in two Rwanda Tribunal decisions, which were apparently confirmed by the Appeals Chamber. I was not aware of these two decisions by the Rwanda Tribunal, but I'm well aware of what the Appeals Chamber may have said regarding expert witnesses. This Tribunal is a Tribunal to which expert witnesses are called upon request by the Prosecution. Sometimes they're even employees of the OTP. So, as to impartiality, there can be a problem. But apparently this situation did not upset anybody, has not upset anybody so far. Everybody works that way, because these individuals are regarded as experts called by the parties, except that experts make a solemn declaration and based on that anything they may say is under oath. Therefore, they become unbiased. The advantage of cross-examination is precisely that the cross-examining party can challenge that impartiality. Second topic you raised, that of Ms. Kandic. Let us move to private session for a few moments because I'd like to mention something that can only be mentioned in private session. Yes, Ms. Dahl, did you want to say something about Ms. Kandic?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, and I'll wait until we're in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're now in open session. Let me deal with the third topic now, which is the issue of the subpoenas. Indeed, the Prosecutor expressed some requests which are now being considered by the Trial Chamber. Decisions are about to be issued very shortly. They have being finalised; therefore, I'm putting this issue aside for the time being because the decisions have not yet been filed. Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If I may summarize our position on the issue of whether a witness can avoid a subpoena by declaring himself to be a Defence witness, I would state just briefly that witnesses are not competent to determine or choose when they appear before the Trial Chamber. That is a matter for the Trial Chamber's subpoena issued upon motion of the Prosecution. The Prosecution bears the burden of proof, and it is incumbent upon us to prove during our case in chief all relevant evidence within the time allowed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber has listened to what the parties have to say about this matter; and in our upcoming decisions, the Trial Chamber will deal with this matter and express itself on the matter. And, fourthly, very briefly, as far as 92 bis is concerned, 92 ter, and 92 quater, as you said, Mr. Seselj, we rendered a decision about an entire series of requests and we have to rule on this pursuant to a number of 92 bis requests. I think my colleagues are in the same frame of mind as I am. Before a 92 bis statement is accepted, this statement has to complete or support elements that have already been received viva voce, and it's only then that we can move on to the 92 bis or 92 -- the 92 bis procedure. 92 ter, well, we don't have to go back to that. We've dealt with it. 92 quater, I'll deal with that rapidly. This is a case when a witness is unable to appear because he is deceased or because he's not in a condition to or she is not in a condition to appear; and given the very particular circumstances, the Trial Chamber can then decide to admit the written statement pursuant to 92 quater, because we have also had other situations. The Chamber heard witnesses, there was the examination-in-chief, the cross-examination, and this testimony directly concerns the case, but that's the other series of documents. But 92 bis, as far as that is concerned, we are waiting to have live witnesses to see whether 92 bis requests fulfil the conditions provided for in 92 bis. That's what I wanted to say. We'll now call the witness into the courtroom so that the witness can take the solemn declaration and so that we can commence with the examination-in-chief. Yes, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, very briefly I wanted to reject the argument of Mr. Seselj that the Prosecution could not be trusted with witness statements. I draw a different inference from the difficulties of Mr. Stoparic's presentation of his evidence. I note that he appeared very distressed in the courtroom; and if you want further submissions on that matter, we would need to go into private session. But we'd ask if the Chamber is going to wait for further ruling -- further submissions in writing by Mr. Seselj on the remaining applications, because we do wish to put in a motion to certify the issue for appeal because we think it meets both prongs for an interlocutory appeal during the trial itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To certify for appeal, what appeal, Ms. Dahl?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: The decision to exclude our motions under 92 ter and 92 quater. The Chamber will recall that the Prosecution elected not to proceed under 92 bis and indicated at the Pre-Trial Conference and at many Status Conferences that we would bring all of our witnesses for cross-examination and that we would not attempt with -- anyway with living witnesses to have Mr. Seselj forego an opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses. Obviously, the 92 quater procedure presents a different matter; but as a distinct legal issue, we think that one is worthy of appellate review; and as of the 92 ter that have been finally rejected, we would like to have that reviewed as well. We are preparing the motions to re-visit those witnesses' statements identified in the decision where the Prosecution was invited to resubmit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To prepare -- to prepare it, yes. Very well. We'll call the witness into the courtroom. Could the usher fetch the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I say something first of all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to the Prosecution's request for leave to certify for appeal because the deadline has expired for such a request to be made. I don't think the Prosecution has any reason to be granted additional time. The deadline is seven days. There is a seven-day time-limit, and I would like to remind you of Rule 71, which mentions taking statements outside of the courtroom. In 92 bis, 92 ter, and 92 quater, nothing is said about the manner in which witness statements are taken, statements that would fall under those rules. But in Rule 71, it says that: "Any statement taken out of court should be taken according to a certain procedure." I must allowed to attend the taking of such statement, and I must be able to examine a witness giving such a statement, and an official from the court must also be present. He must be appointed by the Chamber. What Ms. Dahl is insisting on, the statement she is insisting on, was never taken in accordance with this procedure. These statements were taken by the Prosecution alone. Mr. Stoparic informed you and myself about the way in which such statements are taken. So it really makes no sense to continue listening to these Prosecution requests because they can't find any evidence against me that would be of any relevance, unless they themselves compile a statement against me. Only something they draft can be relevant; everything else just falls down like a pack of cards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will rule on the matter in the light of the submissions or in the light of what the parties have to say. The Trial Chamber will express its opinion, and we have taken note of your position. Nevertheless, we are familiar with that position. We have been for some time because you incessantly re-affirm it. Yes, Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Very briefly, in reply, it appears that Mr. Seselj has not received in translation the motion for enlargement of time that we filed to preserve the opportunity to seek certification pending the Trial Chamber's final disposition of the remaining applications.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: So, therefore, we are not out of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Good day, sir. Could you please stand up. Could you give me your name, first name, and your date of birth for the sake of your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current profession.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I work at Paris X-Nanterre in the library.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What does that mean, a study engineer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a position that scientific or technical personnel have in French universities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before a court with regard to what the events in the former Yugoslavia, or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. As this is the first time you'll be testifying, I would like to provide you with some information about the procedure we will be following. Initially, you'll have to answer the questions that Ms. Dahl will put you. You've certainly met her already, and she will put questions to you about the report you drafted. Ms. Dahl will also show you some documents that were used for your report. All this must be contained in a binder that you have and that you must have been provided with -- that you have been provided with by the Prosecution. Upon completing this stage, the accused, Mr. Seselj, who is to your left, will cross-examine you. After the questions put to you on the report, he will cross-examine you and there will be two stages. He'll ask you about your credibility -- your credibility as an expert and about the substance of your work as an expert witness. The three Judges who are sitting before you will also put questions to you, either while other questions are being put to you or because we have a document that's important that we want to ask you about or we'll ask questions in the course of Mr. Seselj's cross-examination. But as a rule, it's best for us to put questions after both parties have completed their examination or cross-examination. However, there are some times when it's better for the Judges to intervene. As a rule, we have a 20-minute break after one and a half hours of hearing. If you want us to have a break at some other time, raise your hand and ask us for a break. If you fail to understand the sense of a question, ask the person or the party putting the question to you to rephrase it. Try to be as concise as possible when answering questions because the Judges will assess the relevance and the probative value of your testimony, and this will depend on what you actually said. There are monitors in front of -- there is a monitor in front of you. You have the transcript in English, so everything I say in French will appear in the transcript in English. And, similarly, when the accused expresses himself, you will see the English translation of what he says on the monitor. The parties' submissions will be translated, as you can hear through your headphones. If you have any questions to ask the Chamber,, don't hesitate to do so. That's what I wanted to say by way of introduction; and having done so, I will now give the floor to Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tomic. Let me ask you to take the binder of exhibits and turn to 65 ter number 167.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: For the Chamber's reference, the tabs in the binders today correspond to the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Do you speak the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And do you read and understand it as well?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Looking at 65 ter Exhibit Number 167, can you tell me what this document is?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: This is a proclamation to the Serbian people drafted by the Homeland Central Administration of the Serbian Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Looking at the bottom of the page, can you tell me the date and the signatory to the proclamation?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: The date is the 18th of February, signed by the president of the Chetnik Movement, Dr. Vojislav Seselj. It's the 18th of February, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: In addition to his name, does Dr. Seselj's signature here include a title?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes. The "Vojvoda" title is, in fact, used. So "Vojvoda" precedes the title doctor, "Dr."

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: What is the meaning of the word "Vojvoda"?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: "Vojvoda" is a military leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And can you read the first paragraph of the document?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Shall I read it out in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Yes. We are in a tri-lingual court, so the interpreter will be able to move whatever language you use into the languages we can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute to avoid interpretation problems in -- or translation problems. You said, in French, that "Vojvoda" meant military leader. In line 24, it says"military leader." So "leader" makes me think a bit, because you can be a military leader without being a military head. What do you mean by a military chief, chef?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the course of the centuries, in the course of the Ottoman Empire, there were armed units consisting of Christians, of Serbs. They existed during this period of time, and they were under the command of men who were called "Vojvodas." They were military chiefs of irregular armed units; they weren't part of the army of a state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But these armed bands that had been established against the Ottoman Empire, these Vojvods, were they present in the field of military actions, were they there? This Vojvod, as to be understood as Mr. Seselj, does that mean that he was present in the military field or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was, indeed, present. This title as a Vojvod was given to him by Momcilo Djujic in June 1989. Momcilo Djujic was himself precisely a Vojvod, and had obtained this title during World War II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question was more specific. I asked you whether a Vojvod is necessarily present when there is military action, because under the Ottoman Empire, apparently they were there in the field. Is a Vojvod present when there is fighting or can he be somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, he doesn't command from a distance; he is together with his fighters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He doesn't command from a distance; he is together with his fighters, you say. And in a situation, when a Vojvod is not with his troops, does he remain a Vojvod or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, Vojvods are appointed for their military bravery, therefore, always in a context of clashes or fighting, of armed conflict, of small or major intensity. It is always within a military context. It would be a paradox if somebody was appointed a Vojvod precisely if there was no war situation. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. We'll see later. Ms. Dahl, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question in this respect. You said that Mr. Seselj was apparently appointed a Vojvod by Momcilo Djujic in June 1989. Was there a war already then in Yugoslavia, in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The war had not broken out yet, but there was political tension as to the future of what was then Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, how is it that somebody would be appointed a Vojvod, a military leader, who's supposed to fight in the field if there is no war as yet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The idea in 1989, after all, the -- Yugoslavia is going through a serious political crisis. You can see that everywhere. In Eastern Europe, the end of communism is coming. So for the Chetniks who have left Yugoslavia or have left it after 1945 or at the end of the Second World War, it's for them to re-activate their political programme with a will, in fact, to create a unitary state of Serbs. There is a will, and it can be seen in the very words expressed by Momcilo Djujic at the time. They want to take possession of what they call the Serbian lands, including in the territory of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But is this an issue of a political programme, then, or is it already a military programme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is basically a political programme. Indeed, Mr. Seselj went to the United States in 1989, but he also -- basically, he went to North America but also to Australia. And he held close to 100 conferences, in which he expounded his political programme, which indeed mentioned the creation of the greater Serbia, so a unitary land that would gather all the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, one last thing. So can 1989 and can his appointment be understood as a symbolic qualification rather than a military one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may, indeed, have a symbolic dimension; but this being said, for Momcilo Djujic, he has a project which is to see the Chetniks take possession of the lands that are regarded as Serbian, including in Croatia. So the military dimension is supported by an idea expressed in a political programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to follow-up, so you give a military dimension to a political discourse, but in the history of mankind we have examples of people claiming territories based on political discourses without their necessarily having military action.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, the Chetnik movement is by definition a military movement. Momcilo Djujic in the United States is heading an organization of former fighters of World War II, former Chetnik fighters. So it's basically, first and foremost, a military movement, which may have a political programme, but the Chetnik phenomenon initially is a military phenomenon primarily before being a political one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see more clearly as time goes by. Ms. Dahl, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me have this proclamation marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, MFI P140.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can you tell me some more about Momcilo Djujic and his activities in World War II?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: He was born in the vicinity of Knin in 1907, beginning of the 20th century. He's -- he did religious studies in Sremski Karlovci, and he became a pope in 1933. In 1936, he would found a section of the Chetnik Association for the Freedom and Honour of the Fatherland, so one of the Chetnik associations that existed in the inter-war period. When the war broke out, he got involved in a resistance movement against the Independent Croat State --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: -- and was the leader, the head, of a Chetnik unit of the Dinaric region. In this period, indeed, his unit committed a number of crimes. At the end of World War II, he was recognised as a war criminal, held responsible for the death of 1800 men in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djujic have a programme for the Dinara Division?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had a political programme which, as was the case for most Chetnik units in Croatia or Bosnia and Herzegovina, aimed at creating a unitary Serb state, a state which would gather beyond Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dalmatia, and a fair part of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: What was the basis for claiming those territories as Serbian?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: In the Chetnik Movement's opinion, the idea is to create a state that would put together all the Serbs, therefore a number of territories where they believe that the Serbs are the majority population. So it's an ethnic concept of the state, gathering all the territories populated or deemed as populated in a majority by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Sometimes we hear the term "Ravna Gora Movement." Is that the same thing as the Chetnik Movement?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Indeed. One speaks of the Chetnik Movement, but the more official term was the Ravna Gora Movement based on the name of a mountain whenst the Chetnik resistance was launched in May 1941. So, indeed, one speaks of the Ravna Gora Movement, one also uses the word "Chetnik Movement," but also one speaks of a Yugoslav Army in the fatherland, in that the Chetnik units in World War II were units of the Yugoslav Army. Draza Mihajlovic, who headed the army, was appointed Minister for Defence in January 1942. He was a minister of the Yugoslav government that was then in exile in London.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's one thing that is not very clear in your report. During World War II, this movement which apparently fought the Germans, did they carry out a fight directed against Hitler's troops or was it a fight that aimed at creating the Greater Serbia, taking territories? What is their main objective in 1941 and 1942? Was it to resist the German invader or was it to pursue this idea of a Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was primarily the idea of resisting the German occupier because Draza Mihajlovic, he was then a colonel, gathered a number of soldiers who would not accept the capitulation by the Yugoslav Army on the 17th of April, 1941. So, indeed, it is an idea of resisting the German occupier. But later on the specific political context of the time, for instance, the fact that there was a movement of communist resistance which was developing at the time, this communist movement was aiming at taking power during the war. So we're going to see a political rivalry between the two armies. So from a war against the occupier, we move towards a civil war between the communist movement and the Ravna Gora Movement, even if to start with there was, for instance, in September 1941, there was a will to cooperate between the new movements, but it was short-lived. And as of November 1941 until the end of the war, we have a fight between these two armies. Now, Draza Mihajlovic's movement, the Ravna Gora Movement, is a movement that never wanted to fight on a large scale the German occupier. The German reprisals were very harsh. For one German soldier killed, 100 Serb civilians were killed; for one German soldier wounded, 50 were killed. And, in 1941, several thousands of Serbs were thus killed in various towns in Serbia. So Draza Mihajlovic provided to -- by time, and it was like a policy of waiting until there might be the Allies that would come to the Balkans before they started a large-scale action against the occupier. So they waited for this coming of the Allies that never happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And apart from the German question, you said that there was a political rivalry with the communist resistance which had other aims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Yugoslav communists - and in that, they were not obeying Moscow rules or orders, which wanted the cooperation between the two resistance movements, the Chetnik and the communist one - so the Yugoslav communists wanted to use these events in order to take power in Yugoslavia. They had another view of the Yugoslav state, in that they wanted to create a Federation of at least six republics. The communists did recognise the existence of a Macedonian, of a Montenegrin nation, which was not admitted by a lot of Serbs including the Chetnik Movement. So there were major divergences when it comes to the national question between the two movements. But to answer your previous question more fully, I would say that the Chetnik Movement was initially a military one but it is going to develop a political programme as early as August 1941. It created a national central committee, which is, indeed, the political wing of the Ravna Gora Movement. And its members are going to define the objectives of the Ravna Gora Movement, the main objective being the creation of a Greater Serbia in a Greater Yugoslavia. So very early the Ravna Gora Movement, the Chetnik Movement, defended this idea of a Greater Serbia in a Greater Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Dahl. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let us turn to 65 ter Exhibit Number 4, and if you have enough room on your desk to page 47 -- 46 and 47 of your report. Further to the Presiding Judge's discussion about the political programme of the Chetnik Movement, can you tell the Chamber the roots of the programmatic document of the Chetnik Movement? And by "roots," I'm referring to the antecedents or the philosophers who formulated the notion of Greater Serbia that was then created in the programme of the Chetnik Movement.

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, one of the first ideaologists, say, of the Ravna Gora Movement is Stevan Moljevic, together with Dragica Vasic, who was regarded as the number 2 of the Ravna Gora Movement. Together with him, Moljevic is going to draft a document known as "Homogenous Serbia" in June 1941. Then he was not really yet a member of the Ravna Gora Movement. He was going to be member only in August. He is going to be appointed to the National Central Committee, but the ideas expressed in June 1941 fully tally with those of intellectuals who were part of that movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Looking at 65 ter Exhibit Number 4, can you tell me what is reprinted in this text that you used -- well, tell me what the document is first.

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: This is a political programme for Serbia, for the creation of a Greater Serbia. In this document, all the territories that should be part of this entity which is going to be called Greater Serbia are mentioned. This document defines the means to achieve this goal, and, indeed, the idea expressed in this programme is to create a Serbian entity without any national minorities. That would be as homogenous as possible on the national level; therefore, the idea of exchanges of populations between Serbs on the one hand and Croats on the other hand, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, looking at this document, on page 5 in English, under the heading of Serbia, I see that the idea of religion is mentioned here, where freedom of religion is proclaimed. It is even said that political parties cannot be created on a religious basis. What did this mean specifically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we are in a region where there are various religions - there's mainly the Catholic and the Orthodox religion, but there's also the Muslim religion - we know that the religious factor is a dividing one. In order to avoid political divisions in the country, the influence of religion in political life is thereby limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, if I understand well, this movement did not present the Orthodox religion as the only or dominant religion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There is, indeed, an acknowledgement of other religions, provided the external influence is limited, because it is true that the Orthodox religion has its centre in Serbia or Yugoslavia; but for the Catholic church, the influence can come from the Vatican, so from outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This brings me to this question: Could you shed some light on the concept of Serb population? What does that mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serbs, well, first, are the people who identify themselves as Serbs. To a large part, they are Orthodox. There are very few Catholics or Muslims among the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Catholics and Muslims, in what capacity? You say very few of them, but why were they regarded as Serbs then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Especially in southern Dalmatia, in the Dubrovnik area, you had a small community of Serbs who were Catholics. In Bosnia and Herzegovina until after the Second World War, you have some Slav Muslims who also identify as Serbs, but some will equally identify themselves as Croats. So the Muslim nation which was acknowledged in 1968 in Bosnia and Herzegovina indicates a national group which was then not very well defined yet, because you have part of the Muslim Slavs who identify themselves chiefly as Muslims, but part of them in the first census after the Second World War will identify themselves as Croats or Serbs for part of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand properly, this Ravna Gora Movement, through its writings, sets out the principle that this Greater Serbia or this Serbia can be made up of individuals with various religious beliefs, but you explained that back then the majority of them were Orthodox with the exception of Dalmatia, where there were Catholics, and in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where there were Muslims. Is that the overall picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time, you have a relative majority of Serbs, 42, 44 per cent; the second national group is that of Muslims; the third is around 22 per cent, the Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in this Greater Serbia, as understood by the Ravna Gora Movement, empirically in percentage, how many Orthodox, how many Muslims, how many Catholics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, if we look at different programme documents of the Ravna Gora Movement, it recognises religious freedom and it is endeavouring to create a state without national minorities and without Muslims and without Croats and Muslims in that state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the idea that you are telling us; but when you look at the document, we don't see this idea in the documents, because, on the contrary, the documents we have in front of us do not speak along those lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the first document dated the 30th of June, 1941; then if we look at other documents of the Chetnik Movement dating the end of 1941 or 1942, the political ideas are more clearly defined and the idea of a Greater Serbia in which there would be no national minorities and in which the Muslim issue would be regulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we will see this more clearly as we move on. Madam Dahl. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that there has been some confusion intentionally. The Prosecution has not provided the original of Stevan Moljevic's text from 1941. The Prosecution has provided a collection of texts which the authors have called the United Serb Lands, the Ravna Gora National Programme. The authors are Milan Besovic and Kosta Nikolic, and this collection was published in Belgrade in 1996. I wish to remind you that the witness himself told you that when this text was written, Stevan Moljevic did not belong to the Chetnik Movement; he joined two months later. This is the personal text of Stevan Moljevic published in a magazine and not the official programme. And had the Prosecution provided you with a photocopy of the original text, you would see from which publication it was taken and what the date is. The Prosecution does this tendentiously, a brochure from 1996 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I understand what you are telling us. Mr. Witness, you have heard what Mr. Seselj said. The documents in this binder have been drawn from publication dated 1996. So the accused tells us that the original programme is not there. What would be your comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the document itself, it is a study of the national programme of the Ravna Gora Movement, carried out by two Belgrade university academics. So it was a very serious study which presented a compilation of documents relating to the national Serb programme during the Second World War. As I noted a moment ago, this was a document drafted at the time by Stevan Moljevic, who was still not linked to the Ravna Gora Movement. He became in August 1941 as a member of the Central National Committee; and he will become later on, as of 1943, number 2 of the Dragica Vasic movement who will withdraw; and he will, in fact, become the main ideologue of the movement, who will be able to promote his political ideas which were shared by a large number of intellectuals, members of the Ravna Gora Movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but you're not answering the question nor the remark by Mr. Seselj. This Ravna Gora Movement of which Stevan Moljevic became a member, and the document in front of us is a document by Moljevic. Is there an official programme of the Ravna Gora Movement in 1941 or the writings of Stevan Moljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the summer of 1941, the intellectual committee of politicians who supported the Draza Mihajlovic movement in Belgrade will prepare a political programme which specified that the objective was the creation of a united Serb state, in which there would be no national minorities. And we will find elements of this programme in the documents of the command of the Ravna Gora Movement a few months later and in a directive dated December 1941 by the command of the Ravna Gora Movement, and it is addressed to military leaders of Montenegro, Djordje Lasic and Pavle Djurisic. And, in that document, we find definitions of the principle objectives of the movement; the creation of a Greater Serbia in a Greater Yugoslavia. One cannot say that there's a single document which was drafted to help understand the Ravna Gora Movement. We are obliged to take into consideration the documents emanating from the Ravna Gora command and the correspondence between members of the National Central Committee of Intellectuals linked to the movement, and also we have to take into account the press which was -- the press writings by this movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in -- I get the impression that there were two important documents, the one in summer made by the Ravna Gora committee, which is a political programme. And this text, does it appear in the documents in front of us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The political programme from the summer of 1941 drafted by the Ravna Gora committee. Does this document exist? Is it in our list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the list that I have prepared?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, which the Prosecutor has included in its binder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is mentioned in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is a document that you have seen. And a second, which according to you is important, is the directive dated December 1941 addressed to military leaders. Is this directive in the Prosecution binder or is it a document that you have seen in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a document that I have seen, and it is a well-known document by historians. It is a classical document when studying the history of the Ravna Gora Movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this directive, is it in the binder or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How come that two documents that are important are not included in the binder submitted to the Judges for their appreciation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But they appear in my report; they are clearly mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that is your answer; however, the accused is challenging this. And, therefore, I would have preferred to compare this political programme with document number 4, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two other points to make which are very important for these proceedings to be correct. The witness himself said that a group of Belgrade intellectuals worked on a programme. He said that they were close to the movement, but they were never members of the movement. So a group of intellectuals sat down and put their thoughts on paper. There's no official evidence of this. The Witness also mentions a non-existent document. If that document would have existed, he would have brought it, but he's referring to a forgery prepared by the communists during the trial of Draza Mihajlovic. It is an alleged directive of Mihajlovic to Djurisic. There's another forgery, an order sent to Draza Mihajlovic on the execution of Muslims in Foca. Both documents were forged by the communists; they never existed. As they have not been produced, it is clear that the Prosecution is avoiding a discussion of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very difficult to follow Mr. Seselj, who has encyclopedic knowledge and he has so many facts in mind. So it is difficult for me to understand what he is saying. The directive, if that is the one he is referring to, was apparently fabricated by the communists and that was produced during a trial. Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us say that, during the 1990s, there was an attempt to re-evaluate the Ravna Gora Movement, and certain authors did say that a certain number of documents were seized by the communists at the end of the war, and these documents were seized by the communists, the Ravna Gora Movement documents. In most of the studies devoted to this movement that I have read, I never saw any discussions about the directive of the 20th of December, 1941. There was a debate concerning another document I mentioned produced by the Belgrade group, but the real discussion that I am aware of concerns this first document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll certainly see things more clearly as we move on, because this is all extremely complicated. Madam, you have the floor. I see the registrar, who is telling me that it is 10.00, and we need to have a break, as we started at 8.30. Yes, Madam Dahl, you have something to say before the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If I may very briefly simply have this document mentioned by Mr. Moljevic marked for identification, so that we can eliminate that housekeeping detail when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to have a 20-minute break now. One moment. The registrar must give us the number again because it was not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, MFI P141.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now we see it in the transcript. We'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. For the benefit of the interpreters, when using French, we must make pauses between questions and answers; otherwise, there may be problems. So we have to discipline ourselves. Madam Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before the break, the Presiding Judge put a question to the witness regarding the evidence selected in the binder that we were discussing with him. That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must ask the French booth to put on their microphones because I can't hear them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat my question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I understood. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: We have not included on our exhibit list of the documents selected and examined by Mr. Tomic in his historical analysis of the Greater Serbia ideology. If there's a particular document that the Chamber would like to examine in its original state, I'm happy to provide it. Over the break, I counted the number of sources in Mr. Tomic's bibliography at 114, and we would be happy to provide any further information that the Chamber deems relevant. There is a substantial amount of material quoted in Mr. Tomic's report, and it was my considered judgement that that was sufficient to bring the information to the Chamber, and I will confirm with Mr. Tomic how he selected documents for inclusion in his study.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, before the break, Mr. Seselj raised a position that the -- some of the material regarding Draza Mihajlovic was not authentic. Can you tell me how you selected documents to rely on in preparation of your expert report?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: I used archival documents during the communist period. There were collections regarding the Ravna Gora Movement. I used works relating to or studies regarding the national movement of Ravna -- the national programme of the Ravna Gora Movement; also, and specifically, work analysing the press of the Ravna Gora Movement; and here we find a selection of articles coming from various Chetnik units at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can you compare for me the difference between historical analysis of an event and a political analysis?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please? I didn't quite get it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can you compare for me an analysis of an event or a set of documents that has historical purpose in the analysis, as opposed to the achievement of a political objective in the analysis of the event or set of documents?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Regarding the Ravna Gora Movement, one must bear in mind it is not a political party; it is a military movement that has a political dimension. But in the first place, it is a military movement; and, therefore, when one analyses this movement --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let me see if I can clarify. You said before that in the early 1990s, there were some studies that were questioning documents and that you were familiar with them. Were those studies motivated by political objectives?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: What we can say is that the history of the Ravna Gora Movement during the communist period was described by the victors, by the communists; therefore, there was no objective treatment of the Ravna Gora Movement. However, after 1990, when there was a change in Serbia, there was a series of works which appeared, which are again not more objective. There was a tendency to rehabilitate the Ravna Gora Movement. But again, we don't have any guarantee of the objectivity of those studies to the extent that authors wished to portray that movement in the best possible light, and especially certain dimensions of that movement. Therefore, when one is a historian, one cannot always be sure of finding the truth because this is a subject which provokes passions, not by the actual participants because they are less and less numerous, but by historians who have different views on the issue. Having said that, certain documents are false, as has been said, but this does not affect the principle -- main principles of the Ravna Gora Movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this connection I looked at your report and this directive of the 20th of December, 1941, addressed to Major Lazic, commander of Chetnik units of the Yugoslav Army in Montenegro, and Captain Djuric, commander of a Chetnik unit in Lim, again in Montenegro. The fourth objective is important, and I read it: "The cleansing of the territory of the state of all national minorities and non-national elements." This sentence in itself is terrible. But at the bottom of the page, you see again a document by two authors, Dedijer and Miletic. In the footnote, this document is referred to. Did you ask yourself whether this is authentic? Because you yourself said a moment ago that Ravna Gora Movement was analysed under the communist regime and therefore anything is possible. And when you saw this document, did you ask yourself: Was there perhaps a manipulation? Is it true? Is it false? Because it appears as such in your report. And I must add that in support of this document, you add at the bottom that: "Similar objectives were also expressed in the programme of the Dinaric division in March 1942." When one reads this, one has the impression that the cleansing of the territory of all national minorities is a very specific instruction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's quite true that I didn't investigate the authenticity of this document that is referred to in numerous studies on Ravna Gora, and that is because the ideas expressed in document are ideas that were shared by numerous intellectuals and politicians from the 1930s onwards. On an official level in Yugoslavia or in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, in the course of the 1930s, there was even the desire to reduce the weight of national minorities in Yugoslavia. From the 1930s onwards, the Yugoslav government wanted to conclude an agreement with Turkey, an agreement on the departure of about 200.000 Muslims from Yugoslavia to Turkey. This agreement was concluded in 1938 after numerous years of negotiation. It wasn't applied, given that it posed numerous practical problems: How to move, for example, 200.000 individuals; who's to pay for the train to Thessalonika; who would organize the transport. The Second World War then broke out and this programme, this agreement, never came to light, was never implemented. But as of the 1930s, there was a predominant idea in Yugoslavia according to which it was necessary to reduce the number of ethnic minorities who represented 16, 17 per cent of the population in 1928. If you have ethnic minorities within a state, other states could make use of these ethnic minorities in order to destabilize the state in question. So these are ideas that we can find at an official level, at a political level, and these ideas are shared by a certain number of intellectuals who gathered within an organization named the Serbian Cultural Club.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this idea of ethnic cleansing goes back to the 1930s then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that at the time there was an exchange of population between Turkey and Greece after the First World War; and in a certain number of European countries, this exchange was regarded as a possible solution to deal with the problem of ethnic minorities. So at the time, in certain circles, this idea of a population exchange wasn't thought to be shocking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj had something he wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have noticed that the witness is expanding the scope of his expert report, of its contents, and I insist that he bring the secret document tomorrow, the document that was an agreement between the Government of Yugoslavia and Turkey, a document on moving 200.000 Muslims to Turkey. He should bring this document because I am claiming that this is fabricated. The agreement was based on the desire of the Muslims and the Albanians, and that was after the 1920s. After the war in Greece, they wanted them to move to Turkey. The government helped those who wanted to be helped, but they tried to persuade them to remain in Yugoslavia. Nevertheless, this is being fabricated by the witness, and I insist on the witness obtaining the document. He says it is secret, but this is a non-existent document. He says this from the 1930s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This agreement between Turkey and Yugoslavia in the 1930s, the agreement on moving 200.000 Muslims to another country, to Turkey, do you have this document since its objectives are being contested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the document itself, but I do have an article, a study, carried out by a Belgrade historian, I think, a Serbian historian in any event, and he's looked into the matter. He looked into the movement of Muslims from Yugoslavia to Turkey at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His name is Jovanovic. I would have to check this, but it's a recent study that appeared in a collective work that I have here with me in The Hague, and I can bring it here tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Bring it here tomorrow then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the 1930s, the Muslims, were they perceived as a religious group, as a minority religious group perhaps in Serbia, or were they perceived as an ethnic group, as was the case later on? They now perceived as an ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we talk about Muslims in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, it's necessary to make a distinction between several groups of populations. First of all, we have the Muslim Slavs. They spoke Serbo-Croat at the time, that's what we called it; and then there are the Muslims who come from ethnic minorities, Albanians for the most part but there is also a Turkish Muslim minority which is quite numerous in Macedonia in particular and also to a certain extent in Kosovo. Between the two world wars, the Muslim Slavs were represented by a political party, the Muslim Organization of Yugoslavia, and this party cooperated with most of the governments at the time. And one could, generally speaking, say that these Muslim Slavs, or rather, the Muslims of Bosnia and Herzegovina, were not concerned by this agreement between Yugoslavia and Turkey. This agreement, this treaty concerned exclusively the Kosovo and Macedonian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Let me ask the registrar to bring up on the screen 65 ter number 4126.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, let me ask you to turn to map 7 in your report. Can you tell me what this map is?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, in fact, this is a map from the work that we referred to a while ago. It's on the national programme of the Ravna Gora Movement, and this map also comes from a study by Tomasevich on the Chetniks. It's the history of the Ravna Gora Movement. It represents -- this map represents a Greater Serbia within a Greater Yugoslavia, because, in fact, the Ravna Gora Movement wanted to establish a Greater Serbia but it also wanted to extend the territory of Yugoslavia at the expense of Bulgaria, Romania, Hungary, Austria, and of Italy.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can I have this map at 65 ter number 4126 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, MFI P142.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, I insist on the witness stating his position clearly. He should say what this map is. Is this a Ravna Gora Movement map or is it the personal map of Stevan Moljevic? We should know where this map was published and when. It's important for the witness to give us precise information. We don't just want to hear stories without any connection from him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the map on the screen again because it's disappeared now. Very well. Witness, as for the origin of this map, does it come from the Ravna Gora Movement, someone else? What could you tell us for certain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a map, in fact, that must have been based on the Stevan Moljevic document that -- what he puts forward is something put forward in the Ravna Gora Movement. The idea of a Greater Serbia isn't just his idea; it's an idea shared by most of the leaders of this movement. And from the end of the 1930s, there are intellectuals who want to create a Serbian entity within the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, and these intellectuals include Stevan Moljevic and Dragica Vasic, and we can find them as part of the political movement of the Ravna Gora Movement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I have a look at this map, if I have understood everything correctly, Greater Serbia, according to the authors of the map, is the entity we see depicted here. There are certain zones that are in shadow, but they are supposed to be part of the -- of Greater Serbia. For example, if we have a look at Romania, I can see Timisoara. Everybody has heard of Timisoara, so that would be part of Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be -- well, it would be added. This is territory, contiguous. It would become part of Greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is the Banat region and there is a Serbian minority that lives there, so the idea was to attach, to Serbian territory, Romanian or Bulgarian territory inhabited by Serbs, where Serbs would be more or less in the majority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they have a religion, a culture; those Serbs they have a religion and a culture. What criteria is being followed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they are Serbs, that's why this territory would be attached. There's a national minority in the Romanian Banat, and this is a geographic area divided between these two countries, between Serbia and Romania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying they are Serbs themselves. Can you tell me how one can identify a Serb? What are the criteria that allows one to say someone is a Serb, a Croat, or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Serbs are Orthodox but they would also identify themselves as Serbs. Croats are Catholic. It's true that religion is a very important factor that allows one to distinguish them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have religion. What else? What other criteria?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there's an idea of a common national identity, the feeling of belonging to a historical community. That's the case since the Middle Ages. Perhaps one has the feeling of having certain experiences. The Serbs in those regions are Serbs who must have fled from parts of southern Serbia, Kosovo, Macedonia, during the Ottoman rule. They settled in south of Hungary and that later became part of Romania.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the Italian element, why would they be Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in this case, it's not a matter of attaching this territory to Slovenia, in fact, or to Croatia. This is territory inhabited either by Croats or Slovenes. So, in this case, Serbian interests aren't being taken into consideration; the interests of Slovenes or Croats are, however.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So even people who aren't Serbs could be considered as belonging to a Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in fact, as far as the territory in Austria and Italy is concerned, it's a matter of attaching to a Greater Yugoslavia these -- this territory inhabited by Slovenian minorities. So, in the project of Greater Yugoslavia, one didn't only take into consideration the interests of the Serbs, the national interests of the Serbs, but also the national interests of the Slovenes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understood you correctly, in the concept of a Greater Yugoslavia, we had a Greater Serbia that is part of a Greater Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's a matter of establishing a federal state with three entities, three federal units: A very large federal unit which would be Serbia; a smaller unit, which would be Croatia; and there would be a federal unit, a Slovenian unit that would be extended to a large extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood this correctly, the map that I have before me represents a Greater Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, within the Ravna Gora Movement, the idea is to have a Greater Serbia and a Greater Yugoslavia. One believed that a Greater Yugoslavia would be big and important state within the Balkans, and each component entity, the Serbian entity, the Croatian entity, and the Slovene entity, would thus be in a position to oppose the so-called imperial aspirations of neighbouring states. Similarly, there was the idea of having a state sufficiently strong, that would be sufficiently strong in the region, because Stevan Moljevic also speaks about the hegemony of a Greater Serbia and Greater Yugoslavia in the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I must yet again insist on having the witness saying whether this is an official map from the Ravna Gora Movement or is it a private map based on Stevan Moljevic's ideas, a map that was perhaps supported by some other intellectuals whose identity we do not know. This is something the witness should inform us about; otherwise, everything will be confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. There's no confusion. I think he's already provided an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can be more specific. In January 1944, there was a congress in the village of Ba in Serbia, which gathered not only the Ravna Gora Movement but also some representatives of political parties. During that congress, this idea of a Greater Serbia in a Greater Yugoslavia was taken up. We have the resolutions, the decisions of that congress, which to a large extent come from the Ravna Gora Movement. So this idea started in the late 1930s, basically since the creation of an autonomous Croatian area in 1939. The Kingdom of Yugoslavia, during the inter-war period, was basically confronted with the Croatian national questions, because the Croats demanded autonomy within Yugoslavia. In 1939, in August 1939, there was an agreement between the government and the main Croatian political leaders creating an entity called Banovina of Croatia within Yugoslavia. So, as of the moment, when a Croatian entity was created, the Serbs, too, demanded that a Serbian entity be created, which they would name as they wanted to call Serbian lands. As to the Slovenes, they're going to present the same demands; and Muslim Slavs, too, are going to demand autonomy for Bosnia and Herzegovina. So you can see that at the time in 1939, a process has been started of a reorganization of Yugoslavia on a federal basis. Before, it was a very centralised state. One nation alone was acknowledged; that's the Yugoslav nation. But this restructuring started as a process in 1939; however, it did not -- it was not completely done because we had the war in 1941.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is your argument to explain the map, but the question was very precise. This map, does it come from Stevan Moljevic or from the Ravna Gora Movement? Can't you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that it was based on documents that we saw earlier on of the documents written by Stevan Moljevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Established by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By Stevan Moljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a map in front of us. Who made it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was accompanying the text we saw before, because it was published in a journal in 1941. So I think it goes together with that text. But this being said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't have an exact answer as to the author, the one who made this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't have any specific answer on that -- in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Dahl.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, could you read the caption on the upper left-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: "The Chetnik map of Yugoslavia published in a brochure, Nasput, in 1941. The author was Dr. Stevan Moljevic, a close associate of General Draza Mihajlovic. In addition to the internal borders of Serbia towards Croatia, this map implied correcting the Yugoslav borders with all the neighbouring states who were on the side of the occupiers, partly as war damages that were reckoned with and partly because of the unjust delineations in 1918. "At the end of the war, the greatest benefit from the correction of borders were derived by Slovenia and Croatia and Serbia only to a minimum extent because on its behalf Tito renounced war damages which were due to it, either in the form of territory or funds from Bulgaria, Albania, and Germany. "The question of compensation which Croatia was supposed to pay was never raised; but on the contrary, it was rewarded with new territories which is a precedent in the history of wars."

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: You mentioned, in answer to the Presiding Judge's question, that the Ravna Gora Movement convened a congress in the village of Ba in January 1944. What was the intention of the congress?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC
utterances.text: The intention of this congress was to try and get the Ravna Gora Movement out of this political impasse. This dead-end street inasmuch as the movement had been abandoned by the Western Allies. The Western Allies had decided to support the communist resistance movement, which they thought was more efficient against the German occupier. And also --

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Did the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, Mr. Seselj, only raise an objection if it is fundamental. Sometimes you speak but you should do that during cross-examination, because you know when you speak time is lost. And it's either the Prosecution or the Judges' time, and it's not taken away from your time. So only speak if it is essential, if there is a major historical untruth or error, or if you challenge a document. If you now challenge what the witness says, you can do so in cross-examination. Please finish your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In November 1943, the Communist Partisan Movement organized what the future Yugoslav republics' power would be by establishing a federal structure with six republics. You can see, therefore, that there is some urgency for this movement to give an answer to the issues raised by its rival at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj, what did you want to say? What do you challenge? Do you challenge this? What's just been said seemed logical to me, so what's wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm doing my best to make only procedural objections without interfering in the statement of the witness, and my procedural objection related to the previous question. We have been shown some sort of a map of Greater Serbia which is attributed to Stevan Moljevic. Madam Dahl has not provided us with a photocopy of the journal of Nasput of 1991, but she took a map from a book by Jozo Tomasevich, War and Revolution in Yugoslavia. It is a book published in the States in 1975. Jozo Tomasevich is a Croat by ethnicity and an American by citizenship. She is giving us his map and attributing it to Stevan Moljevic. She should have found the original map by Stevan Moljevic. So i think that this is a purely procedural objection. I'm really not interfering in the testimony of this witness. I just insist on documents being described with detail and being told exactly what a document represents, rather than being offered another one, which is not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have this map and then in the upper left-hand corner a commentary. What Mr. Seselj says is that this was a map established by Mr. Tomasevich, apparently an American citizen of Croat decent. What do you have to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
